title: AlphaEarth crop embeddings transferred less well between the United States and India
summary: In a satellite crop-classification study, a classifier trained on US data scored 0.326 macro F1 in Northern India using AlphaEarth embeddings, versus 0.493 using seasonal harmonic features. The ranking also favored harmonic features in the reverse direction, even though embeddings performed better in held-out US county comparisons.
ai_technology: AlphaEarth Foundations geospatial embeddings; supervised crop classifiers
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur; Indian Institute of Technology Delhi; Tata Consultancy Services Research

evidence.tested: The study compared satellite representations on crops represented in US field-scale data from 2017–2023 and Northern India data from 2021, with spatial validation and cross-region transfer.
evidence.unknown: The geographies differ in seasons, sample selection and field structure. The results do not establish transferability to other regions or to all crops.
evidence.ai_role: Learned AlphaEarth embeddings encoded satellite imagery for the classifiers. Comparing those embeddings with engineered seasonal features quantified the regional transfer deficit.
